Definition: Absolute longitudinal slope from DTM elevation differences between segment endpoints divided by segment length.
Rationale: Channel morphology varies with slope, drainage area, and rainfall intensity. Topographic derivatives characterise abiotic setting.
Source: Gregory et al. 1992; Xia et al. 2010; Amatulli et al. 2018; Niezgoda and Johnson 2005

Definition: Mean valley depth from DTM-based valley polygons.
Rationale: Incision depth indicates vertical confinement and floodplain connectivity.
Source: rcrisp (Forgaci and Nattino 2025a)

Definition: Along-network distance from segment midpoint to stream source.
Rationale: Longitudinal position in the network structures downstream ecological gradients.
Source: Benda et al. 2004; Doretto et al. 2020

Definition: Upstream catchment area from DTM flow accumulation; log-transformed for analysis.
Rationale: Catchment size controls discharge and urbanisation effects along the network.
Source: Leopold and Maddock 1953; Paul and Meyer 2001; Bartos 2020

Definition: Road and railway crossing density per unit stream length.
Rationale: Transport infrastructure fragments longitudinal and lateral connectivity.
Source: Grill et al. 2019

Definition: Percentage of segment length tagged as culvert or underground in OSM.
Rationale: Structural openness of the corridor.
Source: Lespez et al. 2025

Definition: Channel path length divided by straight endpoint distance.
Rationale: Planform complexity and habitat potential.
Source: Rosgen 1994; Niezgoda and Johnson 2005; Lespez et al. 2025; Xia et al. 2010

Definition: Percentage of impervious surface within a 100 m buffer.
Rationale: Reach-scale impervious cover predicts biotic condition better than regional land use.
Source: Schiff and Benoit 2007; Sharma and Khanal 2024

Definition: Percentage of tree canopy within a 50 m buffer.
Rationale: Canopy shading regulates stream temperature.
Source: Burrell et al. 2014; Ranta et al. 2021

Definition: Mean width of connected riparian vegetation along the corridor.
Rationale: Riparian width supports filtering and lateral connectivity.
Source: Pace et al. 2022; Hislop et al. 2025

Definition: Length of the longest uninterrupted riparian vegetation patch.
Rationale: Riparian continuity supports corridor function.
Source: Lespez et al. 2025; Ranta et al. 2021

Definition: Mean tree canopy density within the riparian corridor.
Rationale: Riparian tree cover provides shade and organic matter input.
Source: Lespez et al. 2025

Definition: Green land-cover edge length per buffer area within 150 m.
Rationale: Edge density reflects habitat heterogeneity and fragmentation.
Source: Finizio et al. 2024; Jaeger 2000

Definition: Percentage of open or lightly used land within a 100 m buffer.
Rationale: Open space indicates potential space for restoration and public use.
Source: Rigolon 2016; Lespez et al. 2025

Definition: Number of walkable stream entry points per segment.
Rationale: Physical entry points describe direct public access to the corridor.
Source: Lespez et al. 2025

Definition: Total length of walkable paths within a 400 m buffer.
Rationale: Walking and cycling infrastructure supports active access along the corridor.
Source: Saelens et al. 2003; Ewing and Cervero 2010

Definition: Count of programmed facilities within a 50 m stream-side buffer.
Rationale: Nearby destinations and programs support everyday public use.
Source: Saelens et al. 2003; Ewing and Cervero 2010

Definition: Count of public transport stops within a 400 m buffer.
Rationale: Transit stops indicate public transport accessibility.
Source: Geurs and van Wee 2004; Ewing and Cervero 2010

Definition: Mean InVEST habitat quality score within a 100 m riparian mask.
Rationale: Integrative habitat condition variable.
Source: InVEST; Aznarez et al. 2022

Definition: Shannon diversity of land-cover classes within a 150 m buffer.
Rationale: Land-cover diversity as habitat heterogeneity proxy.
Source: Finizio et al. 2024; Aznarez et al. 2022

Definition: Percentage of riparian pixels above NDVI 0.4.
Rationale: Riparian vegetation vigour.
Source: Finizio et al. 2024

Definition: Unique GBIF species recorded within 400 m of each segment.
Rationale: Observed species richness from citizen science records.
Source: GBIF

Definition: Mean total carbon storage within a 100 m buffer from InVEST.
Rationale: Riparian carbon storage capacity.
Source: InVEST; IPCC 2019

Definition: Mean summer land surface temperature within a 100 m buffer from Landsat.
Rationale: Urban heat exposure; lower values indicate cooler corridors.
Source: Zhou et al. 2023; Kim et al. 2008

Definition: Percentage of low relative elevation cells indicating floodplain space.
Rationale: Flood attenuation potential.
Source: Nobre et al. 2016; Verol et al. 2019

Definition: Building origins reachable from stream entry points within 800 m walking network and minimum walking network distance to the nearest building origin.
Rationale: Pedestrian-network access from the public realm to the stream corridor.
Source: Lespez et al. 2025; Ranta et al. 2021

Definition: Public transport stops reachable from stream entry points within 400 m walking network and minimum walking network distance to the nearest stop.
Rationale: Transit-network access to the stream corridor.
Source: Lespez et al. 2025

Definition: Count of program-related POIs reachable from stream entry points within 800 m walking network.
Rationale: Functional program supply reachable from the corridor.
Source: Lespez et al. 2025

Definition: Stream corridor visibility ratio from isovist analysis.
Rationale: Visual presence of the corridor from surrounding public space.
Source: visor (Forgaci and Nattino 2025b); Lespez et al. 2025
